text: ἁλιεύω, I fish.
ἁλίζω, I salt, salten, sprinkle with salt (of sacrifices or of those who offer sacrifice), keep fresh and sound, and so acceptable to God.
gloss: I salt, salten, sprinkle with salt

text: ἀλίσγημα (from ἀλισγέω, read in Freer MS. at Mk. ix 49), pollution, perhaps a polluted thing (specially of food).
ἀλλαχόθεν, from another quarter, practically by another way.
ἀλλαχοῦ (= ἄλλοσε, ἀλλαχόσε, elsewhither), elsewhere.
ἀλληγορέω, I allegorize, I interpret as an allegory.
gloss: I allegorize, I interpret as an allegory

text: ἁλληλουιά (Hebr.), Hallelujah, Praise the Lord.
ἀλλογενής, a man of another race, a foreigner.
gloss: a man of another race, a foreigner

text: ἅλλομαι, I leap, leap up.
ἀλλοτριοεπίσκοπος (a word of uncertain application, perhaps) a pryer into other men's affairs, by means of soothsayers, astrologers, &c.
gloss: a pryer into other men's affairs

text: ἀλλόφυλος, a foreigner.
ἄλλως, otherwise: τὰ ἄλλως ἔχοντα, things that are otherwise.
ἀλοάω, I thresh (corn).
ἄλογος, without (devoid of) human reason; unreasonable, senseless.
ἀλόη, aloes, the powdered fragrant aloe wood.
gloss: aloes, the powdered fragrant aloe wood

text: ἁλυκός, salty, saline.
ἄλυπος, free from pain (grief, trouble).
note: Souter's headword is the positive ἄλυπος, of which the lemma ἀλυπότερος is the comparative.

text: ἀλυσιτελής, profitless, unprofitable.
ἄλφα, alpha, the first letter of the Greek alphabet, cf. Α.
gloss: alpha, the first letter of the Greek alphabet

text: Ἀλφαῖος, Alphaeus, apparently two persons, (a) father of Levi (Mk. ii 14); and (b) father of James (Mk. iii 18, &c.). (Some say = Aramaic Chalphai, and identify with Clopas, John xix 25.)
note: Headword printed with smooth breathing (Ἀλφαῖος), unlike the lemma.

text: ἅλων (= ἅλως), a threshing-floor.
ἀλώπηξ, a fox.
ἅλωσις, capture, capturing.
ἀμαθής (very rare in Hellenistic period), unlearned.
ἀμαράντινος, unfading, fadeless.
ἀμάραντος, unfading.
ἀμάρτυρος, unwitnessed, untestified to.
ἄμαχος (originally a military word), not quarrelsome, peaceable.
ἀμάω, I mow, reap.
ἀμέθυστος, amethyst (a kind of rock crystal: the best specimens are the colour of unmixed wine, whence perhaps the name).
ἀμελέω, I neglect.
ἄμεμπτος, blameless.
ἀμέμπτως, blamelessly.
ἀμέριμνος, free from anxiety (though ‘anxiety’ is rather too strong a word).
ἀμετάθετος, unchanged, unchangeable.
ἀμετακίνητος, immovable.
ἀμεταμέλητος, not to be repented of, about which no change of mind can take place, not affected by change of mind.
ἀμετανόητος, unrepentant.
ἄμετρος (inmensus), unmeasurable, immeasurable: εἰς τὰ ἄμετρα, to a limitless degree.
ἀμήτωρ (lit. motherless), whose mother's name is not recorded (or known).
gloss: whose mother's name is not recorded (or known)

text: ἀμίαντος, undefiled, untainted.
Ἀμιναδάβ (Hebr.), Aminadab, son of Aram and father of Naasson, one of the ancestors of Jesus.
gloss: Aminadab, son of Aram and father of Naasson

text: ἄμμος, sand.
ἀμνός (agnus), a lamb (as a type of innocence, and with sacrificial connotation).
ἀμοιβή, a change, an exchange; hence, plur. reciprocal good deeds (services), a fitting requital.
ἄμπελος, a vine.
ἀμπελουργός (uinitor, vigneron), a vine-dresser.
Ἀμπλιᾶτος (pet form Ἀμπλίας), Ampliatus, a male member of the church at Rome, probably of the imperial household.
gloss: Ampliatus, a male member of the church at Rome

text: ἀμύνομαι (very rare in the colloquial language), I attack in defence, I defend (by force).
gloss: I attack in defence, I defend (by force)

text: ἀμφιάζω (from ἀμφί, as ἀντιάζω is from ἀντί), I clothe, I put clothing (covering) on (over).
gloss: I clothe, I put clothing (covering) on (over)

text: ἀμφιβάλλω, I cast (a fishing net), I fish.
gloss: I cast (a fishing net), I fish

text: ἀμφίβληστρον, a (casting) net.
ἀμφιέννυμι (a survival of literary language), I clothe.
Ἀμφίπολις, Amphipolis, a leading city of Macedonia.
gloss: Amphipolis, a leading city of Macedonia

text: ἄμφοδον, a street, or rather a quarter or block (insula) of a city.
gloss: a street, or rather a quarter or block

text: ἀμώμητος (a literary word), unblemished. (The Greek word properly means not to be blamed, but under the influence of Hebrew the other sense has come into prominence.)
ἄμωμον, spice, an odorous unguent derived from an Eastern plant with fruit like grapes, Rev. xviii 13.

ἄμωμος (cf. ἀμώμητος), (a) blameless, the original sense, which may be that in Eph. i 4, v 27, &c.; (b) without blemish, unblemished, a sense almost invariable in the LXX, of sacrificial animals, and possibly the only sense intended in N.T.
Ἀμώς (Hebr. = Amon, O.T.), Amos, son of Manasseh and father of Josiah, an ancestor of Jesus.
gloss: Amos, son of Manasseh and father of Josiah

text: ἀναβαθμός, a step; plur. a flight of steps, the well-known ‘stairs’ leading up from the temple to the tower of Antonia at Jerusalem.
ἀναβάλλομαι, I postpone, especially I postpone the trial of, with accus. of the person affected.
ἀναβιβάζω, I cause to come up, bring up, regularly from sea to land.
gloss: I cause to come up, bring up

text: ἀνάβλεψις, recovery of sight.
ἀναβοάω, I shout upwards, cry out, raise my voice, Mt. xxvii 46 (text doubtful).
gloss: I shout upwards, cry out, raise my voice

text: ἀναβολή, postponement, delay, putting off.
ἀνάγαιον, an upper room; another form is ἀνώγεων.
ἀναγεννάω, I beget again, I beget into a new life.
gloss: I beget again, I beget into a new life

text: ἀναγκάζω, I compel, I constrain.
ἀναγκαῖος (necessarius), (a) necessary, essential; (b) intimate, Ac. x 24.
ἀναγκαστῶς, by way of compulsion, by force.
gloss: by way of compulsion, by force

text: ἀναγνωρίζω, I make known to again, I make to be recognized (text doubtful in Ac. vii 13).
gloss: I make known to again, I make to be recognized
note: Souter's headword is the active ἀναγνωρίζω.

text: ἀνάγνωσις, public reading (of the law and prophets in synagogue or church).
ἀναδείκνυμι, I show forth or clearly; hence, I proclaim (a person's appointment to an office), I appoint.
ἀνάδειξις, the proclamation of an appointment (to an office); perhaps rather admission to membership of a society.
gloss: the proclamation of an appointment (to an office)

text: ἀναδέχομαι, I welcome, receive kindly; in Heb. xi 17 perhaps I undertake, I assume the responsibility of.
ἀναδίδωμι (reddo), I send up, deliver, hand over.
gloss: I send up, deliver, hand over

text: ἀναζάω, I come to life again, I revive (in Lk. xv 24 text doubtful).
gloss: I come to life again, I revive

text: ἀναζητέω, I seek out, search for (implying the difficulty of the task).
ἀναζώννυμι, I gird up, brace up (with a view to active exertion). A metaphor from the girding of the flowing tunic, to prevent its hampering one in active work.
ἀναζωπυρέω, I stir up the fire, fan the flame of.
gloss: I stir up the fire, fan the flame of

text: ἀναθάλλω, I cause to bloom again.
ἀναθεματίζω, I curse, I invoke curses.
ἀναθεωρέω, I look up at, I gaze up at.
gloss: I look up at, I gaze up at

text: ἀναίδεια, shamelessness, shameless persistence (e.g. in greed).
ἀναίρεσις, taking away (of life), killing, slaying, murder.
gloss: taking away (of life), killing, slaying, murder

text: ἀναίτιος, guiltless.
ἀνακαθίζω (in class. Gk. I cause to sit up), I sit up (text in Lk. vii 15 doubtful).
ἀνακαινίζω, I make fresh again, I make fresh as at the first.
gloss: I make fresh again, I make fresh as at the first

text: ἀνακαινόω (not cited before Paul), I renew, I make new again (cf. ἀνακαινίζω).
gloss: I renew, I make new again

text: ἀνακαίνωσις (not cited earlier), renewing.
ἀνακαλύπτω, I unveil.
ἀνακάμπτω, I return.
ἀνακεφαλαιόομαι (a literary word, from κεφάλαιον, capitulum, chapter, section), I sum up, summarize, recapitulate; in Eph. i 10 gather up in one.
note: Souter's headword is the middle ἀνακεφαλαιόομαι.

text: ἀνακλίνω, (a) I make to recline (especially at a dinner-table); (b) mid. and pass. I recline at a table.
ἀνακράζω (colloquial), I shout (aloud).
ἀνάκρισις, judicial examination, preliminary inquiry.
ἀνακύπτω, I raise myself, become erect (Lk. xiii 11); I look up (Lk. xxi 28).
ἀνάλημψις, a taking up, lifting up (of the Ascension; lit. Assumption).
ἀναλίσκω, I destroy, annihilate (in 2 Thess. ii 8 text is doubtful).
ἀναλογία, proportion, measure.
ἀναλογίζομαι (from λόγος = account), I reckon up, count over.
ἄναλος, saltless, tasteless, flat.
ἀνάλυσις, departing, departure (from this life). (Probably a metaphor from the yoking and unyoking of transport animals.)
ἀναλύω (see ἀνάλυσις), I depart, Phil. i 23; perhaps, I return, Lk. xii 36 (Jerome demands this sense also in Phil. i 23).
ἀναμένω, I await (one whose coming is expected).
gloss: I await (one whose coming is expected)

text: ἀνάμνησις, a recalling, remembrance, memory.
ἀνανεόομαι (regularly a legal word), I am renewed.
note: Souter's headword is the passive ἀνανεόομαι.

text: ἀνανήφω, I become sober again, I recover sound sense.
gloss: I become sober again, I recover sound sense

text: ἀναντίρητος (ἀναντίρρητος), that cannot be gainsaid, undeniable.
note: Headword printed with single ρ, double-ρ spelling in brackets.

text: ἀναντιρήτως (ἀναντιρρήτως), without saying anything against (the request), unquestioningly.
note: Headword printed with single ρ, double-ρ spelling in brackets.

text: ἀνάξιος, unworthy.
ἀναξίως, unworthily, in an unworthy manner.
ἀνάπαυσις, a resting, rest, especially a respite or temporary rest as a preparation for future toil.
ἀναπείθω, I urge by (evil) persuasion, I tempt.
gloss: I urge by (evil) persuasion, I tempt

text: ἀναπέμπω, (a) I send up (to a higher tribunal), Lk. xxiii 7, Ac. xxv 21, &c.; (b) I send back, Philem. 12, &c.
gloss: I send up (to a higher tribunal)

text: ἀναπηδάω, I leap up.
ἀνάπηρος (debilis), maimed.
ἀναπολόγητος, without (ground of) defence, indefensible, inexcusable.
ἀναπτύσσω (euoluo), I unroll (reading uncertain).
ἀνάπτω, I kindle.
ἀναρίθμητος, uncountable, innumerable, that cannot be numbered.
gloss: uncountable, innumerable, that cannot be numbered

text: ἀνασείω, I shake up, stir up, excite.
gloss: I shake up, stir up, excite

text: ἀνασκευάζω, I pack up; hence, I carry away, or dismantle; hence, I upset, destroy, overthrow, subvert (lit. and metaph.).
ἀνασπάω, I drag up, pull up.
ἀναστατόω (perhaps a political metaphor), I turn upside down, upset, unsettle.
gloss: I turn upside down, upset, unsettle

text: ἀνασταυρόω, I crucify again (so the sense seems to require, but elsewhere simply = σταυρόω, I crucify).
ἀναστενάζω, I groan.
ἀνατάσσομαι, I arrange, draw up, but perhaps, as Blass thought, I set down from memory, I restore from memory, Lk. i 1.
ἀνατέλλω, (a) I make to rise, Mt. v 45; (b) I rise, shine (generally of the sun, and hence metaphorically).
ἀνατίθεμαι, I lay (a case) before, I impart, I communicate, I relate (with a view to consulting).
gloss: I lay (a case) before, I impart, I communicate

text: ἀνατρέπω, I overturn (lit. or metaph.) (in John ii 15 text is doubtful).
ἀνατρέφω, I rear, bring up (in Lk. iv 16 text is doubtful).
ἀναφαίνω, (a) a nautical term, I sight (a place); (b) mid. I appear (as it were, out of the unseen).
ἀναφωνέω, I call out, shout.
ἀνάχυσις (probably literary), outpouring, excess.
ἀνάψυξις (refrigerium), refreshing, refreshment.
ἀναψύχω, I refresh, revive, comfort.
ἀνδραποδιστής, an enslaver, one who forcibly enslaves, a kidnapper.
gloss: an enslaver, one who forcibly enslaves, a kidnapper

text: ἀνδρίζομαι, I act in manly fashion, I play the man, I display manly qualities.
gloss: I act in manly fashion, I play the man

text: Ἀνδρόνικος, Andronicus, a member of the Roman church, probably husband of Junia, and a kinsman or fellow-tribesman of St. Paul.
gloss: Andronicus, a member of the Roman church

text: ἀνδροφόνος, a murderer.
ἀνεκδιήγητος, indescribable, that cannot be thoroughly related.
gloss: indescribable, that cannot be thoroughly related

text: ἀνεκλάλητος, incapable of expression in speech.
ἀνέκλειπτος (ἀνέγλειπτος), unfailing.
ἀνελεήμων, unpitying, unmerciful.
ἀνέλεος, unmerciful.
ἀνεμίζομαι, I am blown with the wind (referring to the gentler motions of the air).
gloss: I am blown with the wind

text: ἀνένδεκτος, impossible.
ἀνεξεραύνητος, that cannot be searched into, inscrutable.
gloss: that cannot be searched into, inscrutable

text: ἀνεξίκακος, enduring evil, patient of evil.
ἀνεξιχνίαστος (perhaps from Job LXX), that cannot be tracked out, inexplorable, unsearchable.
gloss: that cannot be tracked out, inexplorable, unsearchable

text: ἀνεπαίσχυντος, not ashamed (of his work).
ἀνεπίλημπτος, giving no cause for accusation.
ἀνέρχομαι, I go up (to the capital).
ἀνετάζω, I examine (a person on trial, a witness) judicially (frequently by the aid of torture).
gloss: I examine (a person on trial, a witness) judicially

text: ἄνευ, without, without the co-operation (or knowledge) of (Mt. x 29).
gloss: without, without the co-operation (or knowledge) of

text: ἀνεύθετος, unfitted, unsuitable.
ἀνευρίσκω, I find by seeking out.
ἀνεψιός, (male) cousin, whether on the father's or on the mother's side.
ἄνηθον, dill (anethum graveolens).
ἀνήκω, in third person, especially of imperfect (cf. Eng. ought = owed), is due, becoming, suitable, proper.
ἀνήμερος, ungentle; untamed.

ἀνθομολογέομαι, I confess (so e.g. the Latin and Sahidic versions), acknowledge, formally admit: I give thanks (so e.g. the Peshitta Syriac and the Bohairic versions, and moderns generally). (The senses I agree, I answer to (come up to), I come to an understanding with, appear in papyri.)
ἄνθος, bloom, possibly a reference to the bright flowers, such as poppies (among the grass).
ἀνθρακιά, a coal-fire.
ἄνθραξ, a coal.
ἀνθρωπάρεσκος, a men-pleaser, a renderer of service to human beings (as opposed to God).
gloss: a men-pleaser, a renderer of service to human beings

text: ἀνθρωποκτόνος (homicida) (borrowed from poetry), a murderer.
